description: Challenge B2 content batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not wired into the live game.

questions.explain: Mischievous is pronounced /ˈmɪstʃɪvəs/ in General American. The standard spelling has -iev- and ends in -ous; the other options are misspellings.
Quandary has /ɑ/ in its first syllable in General American. The other forms are not standard spellings.
Laconic has /ə/ in the first unstressed syllable and /ɑ/ in the stressed second syllable. Laconicity has a different stress pattern; the other forms are not standard spellings.
Tsar is commonly pronounced /zɑr/ in General American, with the initial letters representing /z/. Czar is a spelling variant with the same pronunciation; star and scar begin with /st/ and /sk/.
Phlegm begins with /f/, written ph. Them begins with /ð/, realm with /r/, and flem is not the standard spelling.
Gnostic begins with /n/ because the initial g is silent. Agnostic and diagnostic have an initial vowel sound; nostic is not a standard word.
Lengths ends with /ŋθs/ in careful General American pronunciation. Length ends with /ŋθ/, lenses with /ɪz/, and lengthen with /ən/.
Sixths ends with the cluster /ksθs/. Sixes ends with /ɪz/, sixth with /θ/, and sickles with /əlz/.
Glimpsed ends with /pst/: -ed is pronounced /t/ after the voiceless /s/ sound. Glimpse ends with /ps/, glimpses with /ɪz/, and glimmer with /ər/.
Indict is spelled with a silent c before t and is pronounced /ɪnˈdaɪt/. Indite is a different word pronounced the same, so it cannot be used as a sound-only distractor.
Fuchsia is spelled f-u-c-h-s-i-a. The other options are common misspellings.
Connoisseur is spelled with double n, double s, and -isseur. The other options omit or rearrange letters.
